Chemotherapy for Pets
A diagnosis of cancer can be overwhelming
It’s natural to worry about what treatment may mean for your pet.
Many families are surprised to learn that pet chemotherapy is often very well tolerated by dogs and cats
.
Our goal is not just to treat cancer—it is to help your pet
continue enjoying the things
that make them who they are.
Helping Pets Feel Like Pets
Veterinary chemotherapy is different from human cancer treatment. While extending life is important, our highest priority is protecting your pet’s comfort and quality of life throughout treatment.
What Is Chemotherapy for Pets?
Chemotherapy uses specialized medications to slow or stop the growth of cancer cells
. Depending on your pet’s diagnosis and treatment plan, chemotherapy
may be given as an injection, intravenous treatment, or oral medication at home
.
Each protocol is carefully tailored to your pet’s needs, with a focus on maintaining comfort, quality of life, and as many good days together as possible.
Our Cancer Care
Quality of Life During Cancer Treatment
Most pets tolerate chemotherapy very well, and significant side effects are uncommon.
When side effects do occur, they are typically mild and temporary and may include decreased appetite, vomiting, diarrhea, or tiredness.
Our team
monitors your pet closely
and provides
supportive medications and adjustments
when needed to keep them comfortable throughout their care.
When Is Chemotherapy Recommended?
Chemotherapy may be recommended for cancers that affect the entire body
, such as
lymphoma
or
leukemia
, or for certain tumors with a higher risk of spreading.
It may also be used:
After surgery to reduce the risk of cancer returning or spreading
To slow progression of cancer that has spread
To shrink tumors before surgery or other treatments
To manage cancer-related symptoms and improve comfort
Who is the Vet Oncologist at SERV?
At
Seacoast Emergency & Referral Veterinary Hospital (SERV)
, oncology care is led by
Dr. Kelvin Kow
, a board-certified veterinary oncologist dedicated to providing thoughtful, evidence-based cancer care.
Working alongside SERV’s experienced specialty team, Dr. Kow combines advanced medicine with compassionate communication to help families understand their options and make informed decisions for their pets.
Meet Dr. Kow
Is Chemotherapy Safe for Dogs and Cats?
YES! Many pets continue to eat, play, go for walks, and spend time with their families while receiving chemotherapy.

Pet Chemotherapy FAQs
Get the answers you need from our oncology team.
Is chemotherapy safe for dogs and cats?
Yes. Veterinary chemotherapy is designed differently than human chemotherapy, with a strong focus on maintaining comfort and quality of life. Most pets tolerate treatment very well, and severe side effects are uncommon.
Will my pet feel sick during chemotherapy?
Many pets continue eating, playing, walking, and enjoying time with their families during treatment. Some pets may experience temporary side effects like decreased appetite, vomiting, diarrhea, or tiredness, but these are often mild and manageable with supportive care.
Will chemotherapy be stressful for my pet?
Many chemotherapy treatments are performed as outpatient visits, allowing pets to return home the same day. Some medications are given by injection or IV in the hospital, while others may be given as oral medications at home. Our team works carefully to make each visit as comfortable and low-stress as possible.
Will chemotherapy cure my pet’s cancer?
It depends on the type of cancer and how it responds to treatment. For some cancers, chemotherapy can achieve remission or long-term control. In other cases, it may help slow progression, reduce symptoms, and improve quality of life.
How long does chemotherapy treatment take?
Every treatment plan is different. Some pets receive chemotherapy over several weeks or months, depending on their diagnosis and goals of care. We adjust treatment based on your pet’s response and overall well-being.
How often will my pet need chemotherapy?
The schedule depends on the type of cancer, the medication used, and your pet’s individual needs. Your oncology team will create a clear treatment plan and explain what to expect at each step.
Can my pet still have a normal life during chemotherapy?
Absolutely. One of the main goals of veterinary chemotherapy is helping pets continue being pets. Many patients maintain their routines, enjoy family time, and experience good quality days throughout treatment.
What if I’m not sure chemotherapy is right for my pet?
That’s completely understandable. Our oncology team will take time to discuss your options, including benefits, risks, expected outcomes, and comfort-focused care. We’ll help you choose the path that feels right for your pet and your family.
How do I know if chemotherapy is the right choice?
The best plan depends on your pet’s specific cancer, overall health, and your family’s goals. We combine diagnostics, experience, and honest conversations to create a personalized recommendation for your pet.

@graph.description: Vogel Veterinary Emergency and Specialty is a trusted 24/7 animal hospital in Stratham, NH providing advanced emergency and specialty veterinary care to pets throughout the Seacoast region. Our experienced team delivers around-the-clock emergency vet services, urgent care for pets, and lifesaving treatment when it matters most. We also offer board-certified veterinary dermatology for chronic skin conditions and allergies, comprehensive veterinary oncology for cancer diagnosis and treatment, and advanced soft tissue and orthopedic surgery. Serving Stratham, Exeter, Portsmouth, Greenland, Newmarket, and surrounding New Hampshire communities, Vogel Veterinary Emergency and Specialty is committed to compassionate, expert care for dogs and cats—day or night.
